Eleni —

Thanks for sending this over. Quick context: the credited invoice (INV-9882) was sold by our EU legal entity to BrightLayer EU, so the credit should mirror the original tax treatment (reverse charge to EU). The credit currently sits on the US AR ledger which is preventing our collections team from offsetting the outstanding balance in the EU AR aging.

Laura/Grace — can you advise the correct course for moving this credit to the EU legal entity in our AR? Specifically:
- What journal would we need to reverse-post the credit from Redwood, Inc. (US) to Redwood Europe GmbH?
- Any taxable-event implications we should track for rev-rec mapping?

If BrightLayer is able to reissue to the EU entity that would be safest from a VAT perspective — happy to accept a reissued credit if that speeds collection.

Marcus Lin
Senior AR Analyst

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Credit Note 4321 — reverse charge applied to US entity (requested reallocation)

Marcus —

High level assessment: BrightLayer applied reverse-charge VAT (customer liable) on the original invoice. To correct the posting on our side without a reissued credit we can do an internal reclassification journal entry, but there are two implications to note:

1) AR reallocation journal (recommended if BrightLayer cannot reissue):
   - Debit: AR_US (GL 1200) — reduce US AR balance
   - Credit: AR_EU (GL 1210) — increase EU AR balance
   - Description: Internal reclass of Credit Note 4321 (reverse-charge correction)
   - Reference: FIN-2345

2) Revenue recognition mapping: revenue originally recognized against the US entity will need a corrective revmap entry so deferred revenue and recognized revenue tie to Redwood Europe GmbH. This is a consequential mapping change for Q2 close if we do the internal reclass — need accounting approval.

3) Tax reporting: moving the credit to the EU entity preserves reverse-charge treatment for VAT reporting. If we accept the credit in the US entity, we'd have to do a manual VAT adjustment in the US books and file a correction in our EU VAT return — more operational overhead.

If BrightLayer can reissue the credit to Redwood Europe GmbH (preferred), collections can net against the EU invoice immediately and avoid a corrective rev-rec journal.

I've attached a worksheet with the proposed JE lines and revmap tags. If finance approves, Laura please create FIN-2345 in Jira and tag Accounting for sign-off.

Attachment: AR_reclass_proposal_FIN2345.xlsx

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference

From a collections perspective we need a clean AR bucket in EMEA to apply credits. If we go with the internal JE approach I will: 
- Open FIN-2345 and attach the JE from your worksheet
- Move unapplied credit 4321 from AR_US to AR_EU once the JE posts (please confirm GL postings)
- Update the AR aging & notify the BrightLayer account team that the EU invoice balance will be reduced on 2027-04-06 after the JE posts

If BrightLayer will reissue (preferred), please confirm the reissued credit PDF and I will apply immediately.
